title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Pay When Agents Serve Users? Testing Agent Scaling in Dual-Control Settings
abstract: arXiv:2610.27655v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built from language models are deployed on the premise that collaboration beats a single-agent system (SAS), yet when it pays is unclear. The most systematic study to date gives a capability-saturation rule: coordination helps while the SAS is weak and hurts once it is strong, with the crossing near 45% single-agent accuracy. That rule was derived on autonomous benchmarks, where no user takes part. We test it where agents now work: in conversation with a user under a written policy, on $\tau^2$-bench, the dual-control benchmark. On its airline, retail and telecom domains we compare the stock SAS with a centralized MAS built from the same model for six models from three families, over about 7,950 simulated conversations, with one completion-token ledger per episode per system. translated_title: 当智能体服务用户时，多智能体协作是否划算？在双控制设定中测试智能体扩展效应
translated_abstract: 由语言模型构建的多智能体系统（MAS）被部署的前提是协作优于单智能体系统（SAS），但它何时划算尚不清楚。迄今最系统性的研究给出了一条“能力饱和规则”：当SAS较弱时，协调有帮助；一旦SAS变强，协调反而有害，交叉点约在45%的单智能体准确率处。然而该规则是在没有用户参与的自主基准上得出的。我们在智能体实际工作的场景中检验它：即在书面政策约束下与用户对话，采用双控制基准τ²-bench。在其航空、零售和电信领域中，我们比较了原始SAS与由同一模型构建的集中式MAS，涵盖来自三个系列的六个模型，进行了约7,950次模拟对话，并为每次会话中的每个系统记录完整的补全令牌（token）账本。该研究经过预注册并设有公开的变更日志；MAS按其实际构建方式报告，其中一项有效性标准未达标（其规划器从未见过……）
tldr: 该论文首次在带有用户参与和书面政策约束的双控制基准τ²-bench上，通过约7,950次模拟对话系统检验了此前基于自主基准得出的多智能体协作“能力饱和规则”是否依然成立。
en_tdlr: This paper is the first to systematically test the previously derived capability-saturation rule for multi-agent collaboration on the dual-control benchmark τ²-bench, where agents converse with real users under written policies, using roughly 7,950 simulated conversations across six models from three families.
